quotes.text: Stripe supports installment payments for Stripe Mexico accounts using the Payment Intents and Payment Methods APIs, Checkout, Invoicing, Payment Element, Payment Links, and Terminal.
The card must be a consumer card–installments don’t support corporate cards.

findings: Both captures describe a customer-initiated consumer credit-card payment for Stripe Mexico accounts, with Mexico issuing, supported issuer, MXN and an amount above the applicable minimum. Stripe determines eligibility after setup. Plans and custom minimum/maximum amounts can be selected in Dashboard. The customer repays their bank across billing statements and the merchant receives purchase proceeds net of fees as a normal charge. Standard payout timing applies. The additional installment fee comes on top of the standard card fee (old raw lines 4-56 and 78-101, new raw lines 5-57 and 79-102).

The six table entries remain 3/6/9/12/18/24 months with default minima 300/600/900/1200/1800/2400 MXN and fees 5%/7.5%/10%/12.5%/17.5%/22.5%. These are plan defaults and additional card transaction fees. Configurable thresholds and available issuer plans can still affect offer visibility (old raw lines 78-100, new raw lines 79-101).

Both captures describe display of installments in a hosted checkout UI only after a supported card number is supplied and recommend the same ordering in a custom UI. Card entry and plan visibility establish neither authorization nor capture or payout. The properties list customer-initiated confirmation, recurring, Connect, disputes, manual capture, and full/partial refunds. Platforms can set default installment configuration for Mexican connected accounts and Standard connected accounts can override in Dashboard (old raw lines 22-52 and 62-76, new raw lines 23-53 and 63-77).

The November Terminal listing is a product-level documentation addition. The separate Mexico acceptance capture lists a Terminal link only, so reader/SDK details, API sequence, charge types and operating setup are outside the body read. The May guide already listed the other product routes (old raw lines 8-10, new raw lines 9-11, raw/stripe-payments-meses-sin-intereses-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md:9-18).

Heading whitespace and table Markdown formatting change while the fee values, developer support note and card-display advice remain aligned. The grouping presentation is meaningful for issuer-specific plan availability, including Banamex and duplicated Inbursa, while the Japan UI link mismatch is inherited (old raw lines 62-100 and 102-137, new raw lines 63-101 and 103-150).
substantive_changes: November adds Terminal to the documented Stripe Mexico account product list and changes the property label from Customer locations to Card issuing country. Both captures already state the card-issued-in-Mexico requirement, so the label change clarifies the actor and establishes no eligibility rollout (old raw lines 8-20 and 93-100, new raw lines 9-21 and 94-101).

November groups issuers by supported plan lengths. American Express, BBVA and Nubank are in the 24-month group, and Banamex now appears in the through-18-month group after May expressly restricted it to 3/6/9/12. Newly listed names are Banco Plata, HSBC, Revolut and Ualá. Banco Famsa is listed in May and absent from November; the reason and runtime effect are unverified. Inbursa appears in both 18-month and 12-month groups (old raw lines 102-137, new raw lines 103-150).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the May 1, 2026 capture date despite the -2025 filename. Preserve its 32 distinct listed issuers, Banco Famsa inclusion and the express Banamex through-12-month condition. Date the revised November groupings separately (old raw lines 1-10 and 102-137).

Preserve the dated common fee/default table, connected account override and country/currency/card requirements. Keep UI links as provenance with the cross-market warning, and preserve the path-specific May Checkout and Invoicing restrictions beside both high-level recurring properties (old raw lines 22-100 and new raw lines 23-101).

The November list groups 36 entries and 35 distinct names because Inbursa appears in two groups (new raw lines 107-150). Correct the independent baseline count and date all totals and issuer-plan claims. The 18-month Inbursa entry at new line 131 conflicts with the 12-month group at line 146, so do not resolve its 18-month eligibility from this capture. Carry a reciprocal warning between the mapped source and installments concept.

May labels the property Customer locations: Mexico. November labels it Card issuing country: Mexico; both requirements separately stipulate a Mexico-issued consumer credit card (old raw lines 12-20 and 91-100, new raw lines 13-21 and 92-101). Preserve the identity clarification and avoid inferring either a geographic relaxation or a verified customer-residency rule from the new label.

Both overview captures link the hosted UI and custom Direct API labels to jp-installments URLs even though the surrounding page describes Mexico. The Get started and test-card links do point to the separate Mexico integration guide. Its dedicated November capture is a six-link variant index, including Terminal, while the separate Japan canonical capture lists its own variants (old raw lines 58-64, new raw lines 59-65, raw/stripe-payments-meses-sin-intereses-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md:1-18 and raw/stripe-payments-jp-installments-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md:1-17). Add reciprocal source and installments-concept warning so readers do not apply Japan's accepted cards, products or API examples to Mexico; the index supplies navigation only.

Both overviews show Recurring payments: Yes. The separate May Mexico integration guide states hosted Checkout only works in payment mode, excluding setup and subscription modes, and Invoicing supports individual invoices, excluding subscriptions. Keep these product-specific limitations next to the broad property without inferring universal recurring/subscription eligibility or total lack of recurring support (old raw lines 22-36, new raw lines 23-37 and raw/stripe-mx-installments-accept-payment-2025.md:28-42 and :499-517).
unresolved_questions: The November capture does not resolve Inbursa's 18-month eligibility, why Banco Famsa is omitted, a particular card or merchant's current eligibility, exact installment SDK/Terminal details or operating modes, or actual transaction or payout outcomes.

source_assessments.reason: November materially updates issuer-plan coverage and adds Terminal, while the May source and concept independently overcount the actual May issuer list and omit distinctions needed to select plans and routes.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mx-installments, the November capture describes Mexican installments as customer-initiated credit-card payments. Eligibility requires a Stripe Mexico account, an MXN amount above the applicable plan minimum, and a consumer credit card from a supported Mexican issuer. Stripe determines eligibility after setup. The bank collects installments from the customer, while the merchant receives the purchase proceeds net of fees on standard payout timing. A hosted UI displays options after a supported card number, and the overview recommends a comparable order for a custom UI. Displayed plans and card entry precede a payment outcome (old raw lines 4-56 and old raw lines 58-100, new raw lines 5-57 and new raw lines 59-101). Fees and default minima remain aligned across the six plans, with Dashboard configuration and a Standard connected-account override. November adds Terminal and groups issuers by plan duration. Banamex moves from 12 to 18 months at the top of its documented range, while the duplicate Inbursa placement leaves that issuer's 18-month availability unclear. The mapped source-stripe-mx-installments.md summarizes May's fees and requirements and names Banamex's historical limit, but counts 33 issuers compared with 32 listed in May (old raw lines 102-137 and new raw lines 103-150).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mx-installments, the substantive November changes missing from source-stripe-mx-installments.md are the Terminal product listing and issuer-specific plan groups. American Express, BBVA and Nubank are placed in the 24-month group, Banamex joins the 18-month group, and Banco Plata, HSBC, Revolut and Ualá are newly listed. Banco Famsa is absent. Keep the May issuer list and Banamex restriction dated, correct the baseline count from 33 to 32 names, and warn reciprocally that November lists Inbursa in both the 12- and 18-month groups. The country property changes from customer location to card issuing country while both captures already require a Mexico-issued card. Fee table formatting and headings are presentational (old raw lines 12-20, old raw lines 78-100 and old raw lines 102-137, new raw lines 13-21, new raw lines 79-101 and new raw lines 103-150). The retained hosted and Direct API links point to Japan, while the Mexico acceptance index has its own Mexico variants and a Terminal route. Keep that warning and preserve the broad recurring property alongside the dated Checkout payment-mode and individual-invoice limits. Product documentation, UI availability, card authorization or capture, issuer collection and ordinary merchant payout describe different stages (old raw lines 22-76 and new raw lines 23-77).
